blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — safe injection practices and equipment selection
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — injection equipment selection
educational_objective: Apply CDC patient- and route-specific factors when selecting a needle for intramuscular vaccine administration.

options.A: Route of administration, patient age, adult sex and weight, injection site, and injection technique.
options.B: Use the smallest-diameter needle available for every intramuscular vaccine regardless of the client.
options.C: Choose the needle only from the client's stated pain tolerance.
options.D: Use one default needle gauge and length for every patient because patient factors do not affect selection.

rationale: CDC vaccine-administration guidance states that needle selection should be based on route, patient age, adult sex and weight, injection site, and injection technique, with clinical judgment applied. A is correct.
source_claim_supported: Vaccine needle selection is based on route, patient age, adult sex and weight, injection site, and injection technique, using clinical judgment.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
stem: When selecting a needle for an intramuscular vaccine, which factors should the nurse consider?

blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — monitor laboratory values and diagnostic/therapeutic test results
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — therapeutic drug monitoring
educational_objective: Coordinate therapeutic drug monitoring specimens with medication-specific dosing times so trough results are interpretable.

options.A: At the medication-specific ordered time, typically when the drug level is lowest just before the next scheduled dose.
options.B: At any convenient time because dose timing does not affect trough interpretation.
options.C: Exactly one hour early for every medication because an early sample equals the true trough.
options.D: Without regard to dose timing because the laboratory automatically corrects mistimed specimens.

rationale: A trough level represents the lowest concentration in the dosing interval and is generally collected just before the next scheduled dose, according to medication-specific instructions. NCBI nursing pharmacology guidance emphasizes coordinating medication administration with the timing of peak and trough blood draws because the result is used for dose interpretation. A is correct.
source_claim_supported: A trough is drawn when the drug level is lowest, right before the next scheduled dose, and medication administration should be planned around timed blood draws.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf)
source_version_date: Open RN nursing pharmacology text current as accessed 2026-08-17
stem: A trough drug level is ordered for a medication that requires therapeutic drug monitoring. When should the nurse coordinate specimen collection?

blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
educational_objective: Recognize evidence-supported features of structured transition-to-practice programs for newly licensed nurses.

options.A: A formal program with an educated preceptor, structured learning, feedback, and sufficient time for transition
options.B: No preceptor support because new graduates should function exactly like experienced nurses from the first shift
options.C: An informal program with no organizational support or defined content
options.D: A program that ends after a few orientation shifts regardless of the nurse's transition needs

rationale: NCSBN's national Transition to Practice study found significantly better outcomes when programs were formalized and institutionally supported, included an educated preceptor, provided defined content and time for learning/feedback, and lasted 9–12 months in the studied model. These findings support structured transition rather than minimal informal orientation.
source_claim_supported: Supports formal institutional programs, educated preceptors, structured content, feedback/reflection, specialty customization, and 9–12 month duration in the study.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
stem: A hospital is designing a transition-to-practice program for newly licensed nurses. Which feature is supported by NCSBN study findings?

blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
educational_objective: Identify the types of safety, competence, and workforce outcomes used to evaluate new-graduate transition programs.

options.A: Competence, safety practices/errors, work stress, job satisfaction, and retention
options.B: Only salary satisfaction and parking availability
options.C: Only medication-administration speed with no safety measures
options.D: Only patient census and hospital construction costs

rationale: NCSBN's Phase I Transition to Practice study evaluated outcomes including competence reported by new nurses and linked preceptors, self-reported errors, use of safety practices, work stress, job satisfaction, and hospital retention data. These multidimensional outcomes reflect both practice safety and workforce transition.
source_claim_supported: Supports competence, errors/safety practices, stress, satisfaction, and retention as studied transition outcomes.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
stem: A hospital evaluates outcomes from its new-graduate transition-to-practice program. Which outcome set matches measures used in NCSBN's national study?

blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Physiological Adaptation, printed p.14 / PDF p.18
educational_objective: Differentiate heat cramps from more severe heat-related illness.
rationale: CDC/NIOSH describes heat cramps as painful muscle cramps or spasms, commonly in the abdomen, arms, or legs, after heavy sweating during strenuous activity in heat. Heat stroke is a more severe emergency characterized by loss of temperature control and neurologic dysfunction.
source_claim_supported: Supports painful muscle cramps/spasms after strenuous activity and sweating as heat cramps.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention / NIOSH
stem: A worker performing strenuous activity in hot weather develops painful spasms in the legs but remains alert. Which heat-related condition is most consistent with this presentation?
